provenance.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
provenance.abstract: We introduce a new family of deep neural network models. Instead of specifying a discrete sequence of hidden layers, we parameterize the derivative of the hidden state using a neural network. The output of the network is computed using a black-box differential equation solver. These continuous-depth models have constant memory cost, adapt their evaluation strategy to each input, and can explicitly trade numerical precision for speed.
key_claims: Hidden-layer dynamics can be parameterized as a continuous-time ODE, dh(t)/dt = f(h(t),t,theta), evaluated by a black-box ODE solver instead of a discrete stack of layers.
Gradients can be computed via the adjoint sensitivity method, giving constant O(1) memory cost with respect to depth, without backpropagating through solver internals.

Moving to continuous transformations simplifies the change-of-variables formula to a trace operation (instantaneous change of variables), enabling continuous normalizing flows (CNFs) with only linear cost in hidden units.
Continuous-depth models adaptively trade numerical precision for compute, and this tradeoff can be tuned after training.
A continuous-time latent-variable model (latent ODE) can naturally handle irregularly-sampled time series, outperforming an RNN baseline on extrapolation.

differences.depth_type: continuous but backprop through solver ops

mathematical_spec.name: Loss as ODE solve
mathematical_spec.latex: L(\mathbf{z}(t_1)) = L\left(\mathbf{z}(t_0) + \int_{t_0}^{t_1} f(\mathbf{z}(t), t, \theta) dt\right) = L(\mathrm{ODESolve}(\mathbf{z}(t_0), f, t_0, t_1, \theta))

mathematical_spec.name: Planar CNF dynamics and log-density change
Multi-unit CNF (sum of dynamics, linear-cost trace)

data_augmentation: Gaussian noise added to the bi-directional spiral time-series observations

metrics: number of function evaluations (NFE, compute proxy)
evaluation_protocol.compute: Hidden-state dynamics and derivatives evaluated on GPU via TensorFlow, called from Fortran ODE solvers (LSODE/VODE via scipy.integrate), called from Python autograd code. No GPU count or wall-clock time given.
special_conditions: CNF trained 10,000 iterations with Adam vs. NF trained 500,000 iterations with RMSprop
Error tolerance reduced to 1e-3 (classification) and 1e-5 (density estimation) from a default of 1.5e-8 (sequence modeling)

implementation_assumptions.assumption: MNIST classification experiments (ResNet/RK-Net/ODE-Net) use the Adam optimizer.
implementation_assumptions.basis: Common practice for this era of vision papers; the parsed text does not state an optimizer for the MNIST experiment (only for the CNF density experiments).

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Batch size for MNIST classification is 128.
implementation_assumptions.basis: Common default in 2018-era image classification papers; not stated in the parsed text.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: A faithful reimplementation should use the adaptive Dormand-Prince (dopri5) Runge-Kutta solver as the default ODE integrator.
implementation_assumptions.basis: The paper references the authors' released torchdiffeq PyTorch library (github.com/rtqichen/torchdiffeq), whose documented default solver is dopri5, even though the original paper's experiments used implicit Adams via LSODE/VODE.
alternatives: implicit Adams (LSODE/VODE) as in the original experiments

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Implementation should target PyTorch rather than the original Autograd/TensorFlow/Fortran stack.
implementation_assumptions.basis: Paper explicitly states a PyTorch implementation was released post-publication and is the de facto reference implementation used by the community.

implementation_assumptions.assumption: RNN encoder/decoder cells in the latent ODE time-series model are a standard GRU.
implementation_assumptions.basis: Paper only specifies hidden unit counts (25 for encoder, 20 for dynamics/decoder MLPs), not cell type.
